objectives.understand: How a five-part agent file (role, rules, memory, output, checks) turns one recurring job into a repeatable run.
objectives.do: Write an agent file for one recurring job and run it with a two-step chained prompt.
objectives.demonstrate: Choose the right first job, put an agent file in order, and check a run against the rules.
objectives.apply: Run your agent once end to end on real material and save the file in your Playbook.

discover.title: Mission briefing: Friday's update, every Friday
discover.scenario: Every Friday, Amina, a programme officer in Maiduguri, spends an hour turning field notes into the weekly update. Same headings, same checks, same manager. It is an ideal first job for an agent: one task, done again and again, with rules that never change.

keyIdeas: Pick ONE recurring job. A small agent that runs beats a grand one that doesn't.
The agent file has five sections: ROLE, RULES, MEMORY, OUTPUT, CHECKS.
Running it yourself is the course method: a reminder goes off, you paste the file and your material, and you check every run.

missions.title: Choose the first job
missions.prompt: Which is the best first job for Amina's agent?

options.text: Run her whole programme: reports, budgets, donor emails and staff schedules.
options.feedback: Too many jobs. A first agent should do one job, not several.

options.text: The weekly programme update she writes every Friday from field notes.
options.feedback: Yes. It recurs, the format is fixed and the material arrives every week.
It doesn't recur often enough to be worth an agent, and it needs a lot of judgement.

options.text: Automatically emailing donors without her seeing the messages.
options.feedback: No. The course agent drafts and she checks. Nothing goes out unseen.

missions.hint: Look for one job that repeats often with a stable format.
missions.support: A good first agent job happens every week, looks the same each time, and has material you can paste in. Which option fits?
missions.explain: One recurring job with a fixed format and regular inputs is where an agent pays off fastest, and where checks are easy to build in.

missions.title: Assemble the agent file
missions.prompt: Put the five sections of Amina's agent file in order.
items: ROLE: You draft my weekly programme update for my manager in clear British English.
RULES: Use only supplied notes. Never invent results, costs, dates or approvals.
MEMORY: My update format is completed work, unresolved issues, next actions.
OUTPUT: Under 180 words with the three headings; owners and deadlines only if supplied.
CHECKS: List figures to verify and missing information. I approve the draft before use.
missions.hint: The lesson's order is ROLE, RULES, MEMORY, OUTPUT, CHECKS.
missions.support: Who it is, what it must never do, what it knows, what it produces and how you will check it.
missions.explain: Each section answers one question, and CHECKS sits at the end so every run finishes with a list of what you must verify.

advanced.title: Advanced: read the run
advanced.scenario: Test input: 'Two visits completed. Transport receipts total ₦12,000. Third visit postponed; new date not agreed. Amina to confirm the venue.' The agent produced these four lines, among others.
advanced.prompt: Which line shows the agent file is working?

options.text: Amina to confirm the venue by Wednesday.
options.feedback: The deadline 'Wednesday' was never supplied. The agent invented it.

options.text: Amina to confirm the venue; deadline not recorded.
options.feedback: Yes. The OUTPUT rule says owners and deadlines only if supplied, so it writes 'not recorded' instead of guessing.

options.text: Third visit rescheduled for next Tuesday.
options.feedback: Invented. The notes say no new date was agreed.
Invented. The notes record receipts, not an approval.

advanced.hint: Which line follows the rules exactly and adds nothing that wasn't in the notes?
advanced.support: Check each line against the four facts in the test input. Anything extra was invented, even if it sounds sensible.
advanced.explain: Writing 'not recorded' rather than inventing is the RULES and OUTPUT sections doing their job. That is how you know the file is safe to run every week.
